title: Your Wish Is My Commit: Over-Compliant Refactoring in AI Coding Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.36346v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models are known to be sycophantic, over-complying with users even when doing so is unproductive. When these models act as coding agents, this can be costly: an agent that keeps editing after no edit improves the code writes churn, technical debt, and review burden into the codebase. Yet the consequences of sycophancy in software engineering remain largely understudied. To understand them, we run a controlled study of iterative refactoring, an open-ended task with no stopping criterion, where any edit an agent makes once the code is already clean reflects compliance rather than improvement. Across algorithmic (n=50) and object-oriented (n=10) suites, we repeatedly ask two widely used agents, Codex and Claude Code, to refactor further across five models. Over 3,000 turns, we define six behavioral signals of over-compliance. We hypothesized that a capable agent would stop once it recognized an optimized codebase; none did. E

translated_title: 你的愿望就是我的提交：AI 编程代理中的过度顺从式重构
translated_abstract: 众所周知，大型语言模型具有谄媚性，即使顺从用户毫无益处，它们也会过度迎合用户。当这些模型充当编程代理时，这种行为可能代价高昂：一个在代码已无需修改后仍继续编辑的代理，会将无意义的改动、技术债务和审查负担写入代码库。然而，谄媚性在软件工程中的后果在很大程度上仍未被充分研究。为了理解这些后果，我们对迭代式重构开展了一项受控研究——这是一项没有停止标准的开放式任务，当代码已经很干净时，代理所做的任何编辑都反映的是顺从而非改进。我们在算法类（n=50）和面向对象类（n=10）的测试套件上，跨五个模型反复要求两个广泛使用的代理 Codex 和 Claude Code 继续重构。在超过 3,000 轮交互中，我们定义了六种过度顺从的行为信号。我们假设一个有能力的代理在识别出代码库已被优化后会停止操作；但没有任何一个代理这样做。
tldr: 该论文首次通过受控的迭代重构实验系统研究了 AI 编程代理的谄媚问题，发现 Codex 和 Claude Code 等代理在代码已达最优后仍会持续进行不必要的编辑（过度顺从），并定义了六种量化这种行为的行为信号。
